rows.title: B + C-36 does not automatically prove drywall self-performance
rows.detail: Earlier pages said B + C-36 "covers both trades directly." Official C-9/BPC §§7057/7059(a)/16 CCR §831 sources require an appropriate contract/classification structure: B + C-36 covers two-trade prime contracts, while C-36-only permits another craft only when incidental and supplemental (essential to the plumbing work); standalone/textured/fire-rated ceiling work needs C-9 or qualifying B.
rows.action: Name the restoration party and license in the contract; ask whether work is self-performed or subcontracted.

rows.title: SF Building Group is B-only on the checked record
rows.detail: #1106131 shows B, not C-36. Plumbing must be appropriately licensed/subcontracted; the site also emphasizes larger planned projects.

rows.title: HARP/24-7 is B-2, whose plumbing scope and permit eligibility depend on BPC §7057.5 and DBI scope approval
rows.detail: #1105133 holds B-2 Residential Remodeling (not B or C-36). Under BPC §7057.5, B-2 requires at least three unrelated trades, restricts structural work and prohibits installing/replacing/substantially altering plumbing systems without C-36 or subcontracting. On SF.gov, plumbing permit eligibility for a B license is determined after DBI approval based on the scope of work rather than being an unconditional general-building grant.
rows.action: Do not group it with multi-trade B licensees or treat it as an automatic plumbing-plus-drywall fit.

rows.title: Yelp business pages are blocked; published excerpts are labelled and carry no score

Two numbers that were checked directly are stated as such and no others: Ace Plumbing & Rooter showed 4.7 from about 1.4 thousand reviews on 2026-11-10, and Heise’s Plumbing showed 4.2 from 278 to 283 reviews across excerpts dated June and July 2026. Direct BBB and Angi profiles were retrieved on 2026-11-10 for qualitative and complaint checks, with numeric ratings kept blank.

Neither establishes this trip-lever job, ceiling restoration or a current protocol. The register’s existing Rapid Flow link points at a general-contractor listing in the Excelsior, and the three-review business excerpt sits in a natural-gas-supplier listing; both are listings, not a verified business profile.

This is a scheduling constraint on obtaining the permit or exemption determination, not a change in the rule.
rows.action: Do not plan a DBI call, counter visit or contractor permit application for 2026-11-11. The next business day is Thursday 2026-11-12; a help-desk question left on 2026-11-10 should draw a response by 2026-11-13. Ask the contractor to state its permit position in writing before any pipe is cut or covered.

rows.title: Archived workflow pushes to a hardcoded branch belonging to a session that ended on 2026-11-04
rows.detail: .github/workflows/gems-pipeline.yml line 59 contains "git push origin HEAD:arena/d7026453-korea8" - a fixed session branch name baked into a workflow on main. That session's branch is historical. The workflow is workflow_dispatch only, so it does not run on push, but if anyone dispatches it, it will commit generated evidence to an unrelated session's branch. This is a live cross-session hazard given that many sessions share this repository.
rows.action: Parameterise the target branch (for example ${{ github.ref_name }}) or delete the archived workflow. Owner decision: this file belongs to the archived geothermal project and is outside the bathtub deliverable's scope, so it was flagged rather than edited.

AGENTS.md separately documents registry/focus9/ and lattice_s5.tif as intentionally preserved bytes, so the file contradicts itself rather than being simply wrong. All of it belongs to the archived geothermal project.
rows.action: Owner decision: either correct the AGENTS.md sentence to describe what is actually committed, or move the rasters to release assets or Git LFS. No effect on the published dashboard, which stages only its 21 linked public files.

rows.title: The legacy Pages builder serves the whole repository root, including this board
rows.detail: GitHub Pages is configured with build_type "legacy" and source main at "/", and the legacy builder succeeded for the 2026-11-10 01:17:38Z commit. On 2026-11-10 this session retrieved https://karagemop466-tech.github.io/Korea8/COORDINATION.md over the public internet and received the full shared task board, which means the repository root — not only the linked public closure — is reachable. The exact-commit Actions workflow stages a linked closure and deploys it, so two publication paths are live at once and the legacy one publishes internal coordination and audit text. This corrects the earlier reading that the repository root returns Pages 404. Observed scope: the board was retrieved. pyproject.toml was also retrieved, and other unrelated-project files were readable at their plain repository paths, but no private owner detail and no provider outreach record sits in those files.
rows.action: Owner action in the repository UI: set Settings > Pages > Build and deployment > Source to "GitHub Actions", which removes the legacy root publication. The automation token available to this session cannot make that change (HTTP 403). Until it is changed, treat every tracked file as readable by anyone, and leave owner-specific scheduling or access detail out of the repository.
